description: What the real Parakeet helper wrote for each sentence, and every final text a person would accept. 'said' is what was spoken; 'transcript' is the recognizer's text exactly as it wrote it; 'voice' and 'recognizer' say where it came from; 'accept' is written by hand from what the speaker meant, never from what the program types. 'recognizer_error' marks a case where the recognizer itself misheard: its accept is the faithful rendering of what the recognizer wrote, so the case is not a text-path result. tests/test_whole_program.py dictates every transcript through the real program on a fake Mac as a fresh install and fails when the field text is not in accept; a case with 'known_failure' is an expected failure. uv run benchmarks/recognizer_replay.py record writes the recognizer fields and never accept.
synthetic_speech: Every case here was spoken by the macOS speech synthesizer, not a person. Synthetic speech shows how the recognizer punctuates, capitalises and formats numbers. It says nothing about how accurately it hears a person's voice.
privacy: synthetic speech of public sentences only; no audio is stored in this repository
